problem: Zero-shot object navigation methods lack commonsense reasoning. ZSON and ProcTHOR-ZS still need large-scale navigation training in some environment, and CoW uses CLIP Grad-CAM localization plus nearest-frontier exploration whose decisions ignore scene context. As a result they generalize poorly and inconsistently across datasets.
motivation: Real-world deployment involves diverse objects and houses, and annotating trajectories for them is costly, so agents should find novel objects without any navigation training. Humans search using room- and object-level priors (e.g., a fireplace is in a living room). Pre-trained VL grounding models and LLMs hold such knowledge, but it is uncertain and must still be turned into executable exploration decisions.
key_idea: Ground objects and rooms with prompted GLIP, score goal–object and goal–room co-occurrence with a pre-trained language model, and encode these scores as soft first-order rules in Probabilistic Soft Logic that pick which frontier to explore, all without any training.
insight: Most of the gain over CoW comes from better open-world grounding: GLIP plus plain nearest-frontier exploration (GoW) already reaches 12.4 SPL / 25.6 SR on MP3D vs CoW's 3.7 / 7.4. LLM commonsense via PSL adds a smaller but consistent gain on MP3D/HM3D (HM3D: 18.8→22.3 SPL, 33.1→39.2 SR), mainly by cutting exploration errors (14.3%→10.6%) and choosing frontiers closer to the goal (8.2 m→7.6 m). Object-level reasoning can hurt where objects are placed randomly (on RoboTHOR, ESC w/o Object is best at 23.1 / 39.3), and detection errors (~40%) dominate the remaining failures. Solving PSL over one-hot frontier assignments rather than with ADMM is both slightly better (13.7 vs 12.9 SPL) and ~8x faster (0.25 s vs 2.13 s per inference).
method: Prompt-based scene grounding: GLIP-L (threshold 0.61) is run on each RGB frame with an object prompt (common indoor objects ∪ goal categories joined by '. ') and a room prompt (bedroom, living room, bathroom, kitchen, dining room, office room, gym, lounge, laundry room).

Semantic/navigation mapping: depth + pose back-project pixels into a 3D voxel grid, projected to a 2D navigation map with frontiers. Object box centers and all room-box pixels are projected into a 2D semantic map.

LLM commonsense scoring: DeBERTa-v3 (trained on CommonsenseQA) scores the answer candidates for 'What is a <goal> likely to be near?' and 'If you want to find a <goal>, where should you go?'. Scores are linearly normalized to [0,1] as IsCooccur values; a ChatGPT variant instead directly outputs likelihood scores.

PSL soft commonsense constraints over frontiers: positive and negative rules for object co-occurrence (object within d_o=1.6 m of frontier), and the same pair for rooms (d_r=0.6 m). A ShortDist rule encourages nearby frontiers (weight 2.0 when both reasoning levels are used, else all weights 1.0), and a hard sum constraint enforces ChooseFrontier summing to 1. Rules use Łukasiewicz hinge-loss potentials.
One-hot PSL solver: instead of ADMM convex optimization, the rule violation is evaluated for every one-hot frontier assignment and the lowest-loss frontier is picked (0.25 s vs 2.13 s).

Deterministic navigation policy: after reaching a frontier the agent re-selects one via PSL, and once GLIP detects the goal it navigates directly to it. Extra rules: a long-distance goal policy handles detections beyond the 5 m depth limit on MP3D/HM3D, and on RoboTHOR (no GPS) the depth difference between steps detects blocked motion.

setting.action_space: low-level MoveForward 0.25 m / RotateLeft/Right 30° / LookUp / LookDown / Stop; max 500 steps
setting.privileged: GPS location at each step on MP3D/HM3D (benchmark-provided); object prompt includes the dataset's goal-category list (and on RoboTHOR, common objects drawn from RoboTHOR's category list)

numbers_note: Validation-set sizes are MP3D 2195 episodes, HM3D 2000 and RoboTHOR 1800. The success distance is not stated. Per-category success rates are given only in figures (Fig. 3, Fig. 4). The paper says ESC outperforms supervised THDA on MP3D but prints no THDA numbers. Further ablation variants appear in Table 2: ESC w/o Room and ESC w/o Object; on RoboTHOR, ESC w/o Object scores 23.1 SPL / 39.3 SR, higher than full ESC. Table 5 gives solver ablations on MP3D (object reasoning only).
results: ESC reaches 14.2 SPL / 28.7 SR on MP3D, 22.3 / 39.2 on HM3D and 22.2 / 38.1 on RoboTHOR with no navigation training. On MP3D this is a 284% SPL / 288% SR relative gain over CoW (3.7 / 7.4), the only baseline with the same no-navigation-training setting. ESC beats ZSON, which trains on HM3D (4.8 / 15.3 MP3D; 12.6 / 25.5 HM3D), and exceeds supervised PONI's MP3D SPL (12.1). It is still well below supervised ProcTHOR on HM3D (31.8 / 54.4) and below ProcTHOR-ZS on RoboTHOR (23.7 / 55.0).
limitations: The commonsense gain is modest relative to the grounding gain. Object reasoning slightly hurts on RoboTHOR, where objects are placed randomly.
Rule weights and thresholds form a fixed hand-set combination strategy, and there is no spatial reasoning between rooms. Detection errors (~40% of failures) dominate and are not addressed.
Prompts are dataset-specific (goal lists; RoboTHOR common objects taken from dataset categories). The method is evaluated only in simulation and relies on GPS on MP3D/HM3D.
